labels.label: bzdef:c3s6d1_prolonge
labels.notes: Prolonge l W V := IsConvexPart V ∧ V ∩ openHemisphere l = W ∩ openHemisphere l is the printed definition (« si si » read as one « si »); the context « W ⊆ H » is not built in, which only widens it. The definition's claim (W ∩ H = V ∩ H for W, V closed, H̊ ∩ W ≠ ∅) is inter_closedHemisphere_eq_of_prolonge on any S(E) (topological vector space E), any linear form l, without W ⊆ H: Lean ≥ paper. The paper's E (finest locally convex topology) is a TVS (isTopologicalAddGroup_finestLC, continuousSMul_finestLC), so the general form applies to it. Instance prolonge_self is trivial but the claim is exercised by isClosed_sature / noyau_sature_nonempty_iff_isLeast through the trace lemma.

labels.label: bzprop:c3s6p1_sature
labels.notes: prop1_sature_Sn (on S(n)) carries exactly the printed hypotheses (IsConvexPart W, IsClosed W, noyau W = ∅ with Sphere.noyau of § 1 Déf. 5, W ⊆ closedHemisphere l, W ∩ H̊ ≠ ∅) and concludes: a greatest prolongation exists, sature l W is it (IsGreatest), it is closed, (noyau V).Nonempty ↔ ∃ p ∈ H̊, W = enveloppeConvexe ({p} ∪ (W ∩ h)) — the « sauf si » as an equivalence, so it holds under both readings — and uniqueness of the apex in H̊. prop1_sature is the S(E) form with Continuous l and T1Space E: both hold for the paper's E (t2Space_finestLC, continuous_linearMap_finestLC) and every DEC-114 closed hemisphere has a continuous equation (IsClosedHemisphere.exists_eq returns a StrongDual), so neither narrows the paper; both disclosed in the checklist. h = linearSubvariety (ker l) is the frontier (frontier_openHemisphere). enveloppeConvexe is reused from Chapter2/Hemisphere.lean:240, not redefined; on S(E) the hull is read as IsLeast {k | IsConvexPart k ∧ A ⊆ k}, which exists (convex parts are closed under intersection, the whole sphere is convex) and coincides with enveloppeConvexe on S(n) (isLeast_iff_eq_enveloppeConvexe, proved): a legitimate reading. Step 1° as printed is prolonge_enveloppeConvexe_union (hull of V′ ∪ V″ prolongs W), with prolonge_join the S(E) form. Instances: arcY = {y ≥ |x|} ⊆ S(1), H = {y ≥ 0}, satisfies every hypothesis (arcY_hypotheses, proved: convex, closed, noyau empty, in H, meets H̊) and has noyau of V empty (noyau_sature_arcY); ptY = {(0,1)} satisfies every hypothesis and is the exception with noyau of V nonempty (ptY_hypotheses), exercising the converse direction. Both are non-vacuous.

labels.label: bzcor:c3s6p1c_sature_corps_convexe
labels.notes: sature_corps_convexe: IsCorpsConvexeS n W (strict convex, compact, nonempty interior: the library's Déf. 11), W ⊆ closedHemisphere l for any l (l = 0 included and shown to make the printed hypothesis false), ∀ p : S n, W ≠ enveloppeConvexe ({p} ∪ (W ∩ h)) ⇒ IsCorpsConvexeS n (sature l W): exactly the printed statement, with sature l W the saturated convex of Prop. 1 (its hypotheses are derived: noyau empty from strictness, closed from compact, W ∩ H̊ ≠ ∅ from inter_openHemisphere_nonempty). sature_corps_convexe_of_ne_zero is the stronger form (hypothesis only over p ∈ H̊, l ≠ 0), and implies the printed one. Instance arcY_corps_convexe discharges the hypothesis (arcY_ne_enveloppeConvexe) and is a real convex body.
